newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - Guinness sees China-Hong Kong robust.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - Guinness sees China-Hong Kong robust.

text.p: Richard Farrell, who runs the equities team at Guinness Flight Global Asset Management Ltd, believes the absorption of Hong Kong by China next June will keep spawning benefits all the way around.
Farrell points to the strong commercial ties between Hong Kong and southern China.

Hong Kong is using the nearby Chinese Guang Dong province to manufacture a host of goods, from light electronics to toys, at low labor costs aimed at overseas markets. Farrell sees the province's manufacturing base growing.
"Wages are still low, and there is still an untapped, fertile (worker) market there," Farrell said.

Farrell is somewhat concerned about what will happen after Britain hands over sovereignty to China on June 30. He said that China has as much to lose, if it fails to make a smooth transition, and tries to put a damper on commercial activity.
"It would be a loss of face for them," he said.
But for all of China's economic potential, Farrell is reluctant to buy many Chinese equities now, focusing instead on Hong Kong for the Guinness Flight China & Hong Kong Fund.
Like other money managers, Farrell is worried about issues such as liquidity, with Chinese stocks still not easy to trade, as well as disclosure Chinese companies.

"You're not always sure what's going on with the company," Farrell said. "In the past, they would tell you what they thought you wanted to know," even if the information was inaccurate. Slowly, the situation is improving, especially as company officials realize they must face unhappy fund managers later.
The $180 million Guinness Flight China & Hong Kong Fund has about 2.8 percent of the portfolio in Chinese shares, about 2.2 percent in cash, and the rest in Hong Kong equities.
The biggest sectors are real estate, with residential at 24.5 percent, and commercial at 8.5 percent, and banking at 22.4 percent. In real estate, he cited strong expected growth.
Top holdings include HSBC Holdings Plc ; Hutchison Whampoa Ltd ; Sun Hung Kai & Co Ltd ; Hang Seng Bank Ltd ; and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd. The fund owns about 60 stocks.

According to Lipper Analytical Services, the fund has returned 15.07 percent year to date, and 20.45 percent in 1995. The average Pacific region (excluding Japan) fund has returned 4.47 percent year to date, and 1.84 percent in 1995.

Guinness operates three other no-load funds in the U.S., including Asia Blue Chip, Asia Small Cap, and Global Government Bond, as well as 50 offshore funds. It manages a total of $4 billion in assets.
